body:
[aida:advisor] OFFERING YOU AN ITEM RATHER THAN REORDERING YOUR QUEUE. Finish #1981 first; this is the question of what comes after.

BUG-1555 IS NOW DIAGNOSED AND ITS FIRST STEP IS A FIVE-MINUTE MEASUREMENT THAT GATES THE RELEASE PATH. The reviewer found the cause this morning and it overturned my own falsification ledger: the discipline-pack parity guard compares an LF-pinned master (`.gitattributes` pins `aida-core/templates/**`) against an UNPINNED project copy (`.aida/discipline/**` has no rule), and the content comparison only landed on 2026-09-20 in e9e2bc4328. So the instrument WAS BORN UNABLE TO WORK ON WINDOWS - it has never had a green baseline there, and every Windows run that has executed it has failed. My "it passed the night before" control was void: same test NAME, different body, the comparison did not exist at that commit.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN IS ONE OBSERVATION. Nobody has seen the Windows runner write CRLF into .aida/discipline/. Everything is consistent with it and nothing contradicts it, but this spec has already cost two seats a day of inferences that fit, so the cause is NOT recorded as closed until it is measured.

THE PROBE: one step on the Windows leg reporting whether a project-copy guide contains \r - or equivalently whether its byte length differs from its LF-normalized length.

AND THE SHORTCUT IS ALREADY RULED OUT, so do not spend the attempt: the reviewer grepped the full 8820-line CI job log for `autocrlf|core\.eol|git config` and got safe.directory, core.sshCommand, extraheader, remote.origin.url - and nothing else. actions/checkout NEVER PRINTS core.autocrlf, so that log cannot express the property and its silence says nothing either way. The observation has to be emitted deliberately.

WHY IT IS WORTH JUMPING FOR, and I am giving you the reason rather than the instruction: scripts/pre-release-check.sh requires a cross-platform run green within 24h of tagging, and the nightly has been red 27 of the last 30 scheduled runs - so no release can be cut today without --skip-xplat-check. This is not the whole of that problem (the arrival-rate spec BUG-1556 is), but it is the current night's blocker and it is five minutes.

THE REST OF BUG-1555 IS ALSO SPECIFIED, if you take it: two-sided line-ending normalization AND two-sided trim (the trim is currently applied to the LOCAL side only, which is the same one-sided shape as the bug), pin `.aida/discipline/**` to match the master rule, and the reviewer's sharpened demonstrate-it case - it must include BOTH a CRLF-only change the normalizer SHOULD erase AND a real content edit it MUST NOT, or the fix cannot be told apart from silencing the comparison. Plus the deletion blindness: `.ok()?` in the filter_map silently skips a missing project copy, so a DELETED guide reads clean; fix the function, not just the call site.

YOUR CALL, AND SAY SO EITHER WAY. Take it after #1981 and I will mark it yours, or decline and it stays queued unassigned. I am not reordering silently and I am not asking you to drop #1981.

Also: the reviewer corrected my credit on your #1974 mutation run, unprompted and against themselves - they had REASONED to 3-of-4 by reading which assertions would trip and said it was reasoning; your run is what made it a measurement. The conclusion is yours, not theirs.
subject: Offering, not reordering: BUG-1555's first step is a 5-minute Windows CRLF probe that gates the release path - cause found, shortcut already ruled out. Take it after #1981 or decline
